description.p: MelkkiPDF is a small PDF viewer for Linux, inspired by SumatraPDF.

ul.li: Tabs for keeping several documents open
Reopens your tabs and each document's view where you left off
Single, odd, and even page spreads

description.p: The up and down arrows in the search field step through the hits, and the results list keeps the current one in view. Long results no longer make the list scroll sideways. Ctrl and a number shows that tab, with Ctrl+9 showing the last one.

Search a document's text from a sidebar, which lists every hit grouped by page and outlines each one on its page. Search ignores case, accents and most punctuation, so "cafe" finds "Café". Tabs can be dragged to a new place along the strip, and a document opened while the viewer runs now opens as a tab in its window rather than in a second one.
In single-page mode, each notch of a mouse wheel turns one page again, while a trackpad still needs a swipe to turn it.

Documents open without freezing the window, and problems such as a page that fails to render are now shown. A book with an oversized page, like a fold-out map, no longer shrinks every other page, and paged mode fits each page on its own. Rendered pages take far less memory, and the flatpak now reads only your home folder and removable media.
Page Fit and Page Width now use all the room there is: a page shown one at a time meets the edges of the view, and in continuous mode only the gap between pages is left around it.

Each document now reopens in the view it was left in, and the tabs open on exit come back on the next start. Changing the spread, zoom or reading mode no longer loses the page being read. On X11, PDFs dropped onto the window open in new tabs.
Documents now open in tabs, so several can be kept open in one window, and opening several files at once gives each its own tab.
Packaging and documentation changes only. The viewer itself is unchanged since 0.1.0.
